prediction.likelyOutcome: Brexton should defeat Four Elyria's summary judgment motion — the Galvin/Giltz conflict and Giltz's limited personal knowledge create genuine fact issues on the oral agreement, change-order waiver, and tort intent — but Brexton will not win its own motion and should expect a jury trial on scope and waiver. The most likely resolution is a pre-trial or mid-trial settlement in which the liens are released in exchange for a partial payment, with Brexton recovering a fraction of the ~$500,000 and the fraud/slander-of-title claims against the officers dismissed.

issues.label: Recovery for Site-Specific Work (breach of oral/separate contract and, alternatively, unjust enrichment)
Fraud claim against Brexton and its two officers (exposure)
Defeating Four Elyria's motion for summary judgment
Effect of the unconditional lien waivers on lien and claim
Four Elyria's breach claim for failure to pay subcontractors (exposure/offset)
Applicability of the cited precedent list

outcome.description: The trial court held the Site-Specific Work was outside the contract, granted summary judgment against Four Elyria on all its claims and for Brexton on unjust enrichment, and after a damages-only jury trial entered judgment for Brexton for $465,417.44; both sides' attorney-fee motions were denied and Brexton's lien-foreclosure counterclaim was dismissed. On this second appeal the court of appeals agreed the work was outside the contract but reversed in part and remanded for the trial court to apply the contract's Article 9 change-order provisions, leaving the unjust-enrichment award and the fee issues to be revisited on remand.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed in part and remanded; no final figure yet.
